text.p: British pharmaceutical company Medeva Plc said on Thursday that late stage trials of its Hepatitis B vaccine Hepagene had been positive.
Analysts see the drug as a potentially important money spinner for the company. The vaccine is aimed at individuals who are immune to existing prophylactics.

In its statement Medeva said the trials "provide substantial data confirming that Hepagene is superior" when compared with SmithKline Beecham Plc's Energix-B vaccine in protecting individuals who have not responded to vaccination.
The company confirmed that it would also continue to evaluate Hepagene as a potential treatment for sufferers of Hepatitis B, which is potentially a much larger market.
The company also surprised analysts by announcing plans to file for registration of the product in both the U.S. and Europe in 1998, earlier than expected.

In a telephone interview with Reuters chief executive William Bogie said the move reflected Medeva's confidence over the patent postion on the product. Medeva has been invloved in a complex patent battle with the U.S. group Biogen Inc.
It won an appeal by Biogen to the House of Lords last year, opening the way to development of the drug in the UK, but patent issues elsewhere are still outstanding.
Bogie also told Reuters that Medeva would not be seeking marketing partnerships for Hepagene in the U.S. and Europe.
The company already has an alliance with Johnson & Johnson to distribute the product in south-east Asia.
There had been speculation that the company could form a closer link with SmithKline Beecham Plc, with whom it already has a broad vacccine alliance.
"We are not looking for a partner. That doesn't mean they won't happen but we are fairly confident that we can do it ourselves," Bogie said.
